subject: AI & Agents
title: What Is Creativity, Really?
description: A micro-lesson that makes What Is Creativity, Really? usable.

hook.text: We say a painting is creative but not a sunset. What separates creation from coincidence?

buildup.text: Psychologists define creativity as producing something novel, useful, and surprising.

discovery.text: Margaret Boden identified three types: combinational, exploratory, and transformational creativity.

twist.text: By these definitions, AI already achieves combinational and exploratory creativity.

climax.text: The debate isn't whether AI outputs are creative — it's whether the process counts.

punchline.text: Creativity might be in the output, not the creator.

quiz.question: What are the three types of creativity identified by Margaret Boden?

details.summary: Creativity involves producing something novel, valuable, and surprising. Defining it precisely is essential before we can decide whether machines qualify as creative agents.
details.whyItMatters: Without a clear definition of creativity, debates about AI art remain circular. Understanding what creativity means helps us evaluate machine outputs fairly.
takeaways: Creativity requires novelty, value, and surprise
Definitions vary across psychology, philosophy, and art
Clarifying creativity helps evaluate AI outputs objectively

faq.question: How do researchers define creativity?
faq.answer: Most definitions include three elements: the output must be novel, it must have value or usefulness, and it should surprise the audience or creator. Some add intentionality as a fourth criterion.

faq.question: Can machines meet the standard definition of creativity?
faq.answer: AI can produce novel and valued outputs, but whether it acts with intention or genuine surprise is debated. The answer depends heavily on which definition of creativity you adopt.
